previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for dizziness and shortness of breath, found to be due to hypotension and hyponatremia in the setting of peritoneal dialysis. She had a 10-pound weight loss and worsening nausea from longstanding gastroparesis. Peritoneal fluid analysis showed elevated white blood cells, consistent with peritonitis, though cultures remained negative. She was treated with intraperitoneal ceftazidime, with clinical improvement. Hyponatremia resolved with fluid management, and bowel symptoms stabilized with a consistent regimen. She was discharged home with plans to continue antibiotics via her dialysis center, and follow-up with nephrology and GI.

ACTIVE ISSUES
=============
# Nausea/Vomiting/Diarrhea: The patient's diarrhea self-resolved 
at admission, and although she continued to be nauseous without 
ability to tolerate POs she had no episodes of emesis. She was 
also noted to be afebrile with resolution of leukocytosis during 
her course. Given these findings, it was presumed that her 
persistent nausea was secondary to gastroparesis. She was given 
standing Colace, senna, and bisacodyl, continued on her home 
lubiprostone, given PRN IV compazine, and eventually started on 
erythromycin 250mg PO Q8H for gastroparesis, and her symptoms 
resolved. She was tolerating POs at baseline at discharge. Of 
note, she did have a few episodes of loose bowel movements later 
in her course, but this was attributed to use of excess bowel 
regimen.

# Headache: Potential contributing factors include migraine, 
post-LP headache, and dehydration. Patient's symptoms similar to 
prior migraines although more severe, perhaps exacerbated in 
setting of dehydration.  The patient's topiramate dose was 
uptitrated to 100mg BID, and she was given PRN sumatriptan, PRN 
Compazine, and IV Tylenol. Ultimately she was given PRN 
oxycodone given her persistent symptoms, although the team 
expressed concerns given prior failure of Vicodin to improve her 
symptoms and given that opioids would likely worsen her 
gastroparesis and chronic pruritus. Of note, the patient had a 
documented allergy to oxycodone but could not recall any adverse 
effect, and had no reaction to receiving the medication. It 
improved her headache and back pain. 

# Dizziness/Hypotension: The patient was noted to have lost >3L 
during PD during one day of her course, and her BPs dropped with 
SBPs as low as the ___. She was also noted to be orthostatic at 
this time. She received gentle IV fluids, was encouraged to take 
POs, and had her dialysis orders adjusted, and her pressures 
normalized.

# Back/Neck Pain: Diffuse pain and tenderness was noted 
throughout her spine; with lack of localizing tenderness. Muscle 
tension on exam raised concern for muscle spasm component. She 
was treated with IV Tylenol, as well as her migraine treatment 
as noted above. Lidocaine patches and heating pads were given 
although only provided mild relief. As noted above, she was 
ultimately given oxycodone, which provided also partial relief.

# Subjective fever: The patient noted fevers at home but was 
afebrile during her hospital course. She had leukocytosis at 
admission but resolved thereafter. UA was unremarkable; urine 
cultures grew Group B strep ___ but given no urinary 
symptoms, this was deemed asymptomatic bacteriuria not requiring 
treatment. Blood cultures were pending at discharge, and stool 
studies were either negative or pending at discharge.

consult, with ___ daily cycles. The patient was noted to have a

# T1DM: Continued on Lantus 6 Units QHS and a low-dose Humalog

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___,

It was a pleasure taking care of you during your stay at ___. 
You were admitted with nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea, as well 
as headache, back pain, and neck pain. Your diarrhea resolved 
once you were admitted, and your nausea and vomiting were 
treated with medications for gastroparesis and anti-nausea 
medication. For your headache we gave you pain medication and 
increased your topiramate dose. Your symptoms improved by the 
time of your discharge.

We have increased your dose of topiramate to 100mg twice a day, 
in line with your neurologist Dr. ___. He 
will follow up with you and may recommend you increase your dose 
further.

For your neck and back pain you were seen by the rheumatology 
doctors to ___ if we could further work up your pain. You also 
were interested in acupuncture. We will provider you with ___ 
referral to our integrative medicine program at ___. You should 
continue to use heat packs for your back and neck pain. Lastly, 
you may follow up at our Pain Management Clinic; please call 
___ to make an appointment.

Lastly, we have discontinued your Vicodin but have given you a 
prescription for new pain medication, oxycodone, which you may 
use as needed. Like Vicodin, oxycodone has a sedating effect and 
we recommend you be cautious when taking this medication and 
combining it with your other home medications. It may worsen 
your symptoms of gastroparesis and itch. Please do not drive or 
operative heavy machinery while taking this medication. Please 
do not mix with alcohol. 

Lastly, as we are discontinuing your Vicodin, please return any 
old pill bottles with Vicodin to your primary care appointment 
on ___.

We wish you the best.

Your ___ Care Team
